objects.body: Authors, reviews, and approves engineering objects; reads generated views to understand traceability and coverage.
objects.title: Requirements engineer

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

The product has a Python analysis core, Lua rendering filters, and JavaScript interaction. If each layer defines engineering meaning independently, equivalent views can drift.

### Decision Drivers

- one source of engineering semantics;
- deterministic analysis;
- testability outside the browser;
- presentation layers that remain replaceable.

### Considered Options

- duplicate relation maps in every client;
- resolve semantics in Lua during rendering;
- resolve semantics once in Python and publish semantic projections.

### Decision Outcome

Python owns engineering semantics. Lua and JavaScript consume relation metadata and other semantic projections emitted by the core.

### Consequences

Public projection contracts become more important, but presentation clients become simpler and cannot silently redefine engineering meaning.

### Confirmation

`TC-001` confirms the canonical snapshot and `TC-008` confirms relation-catalog semantics.
objects.title: Keep Python as the semantic authority

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

The engineering model needs both formal structure and high-quality human explanation.

### Decision Drivers

- text and Git workflows;
- publishable documentation;
- Markdown narrative;
- extension-based generated views.

### Decision Outcome

Use Quarto documents as the authoring and publishing interface while keeping engineering semantics in the Python core.

### Consequences

The product remains compatible with ordinary documentation workflows and can progressively enhance HTML without making HTML the source of truth.

### Confirmation

`TC-002` renders the book and verifies the static/progressive presentation path.
objects.title: Use Quarto as the executable documentation interface

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

Requirements, decisions, risks, implementation, tests, and evidence need a common relationship model without collapsing their distinct meanings.

### Decision Outcome

Represent engineering objects as typed nodes and engineering relations as typed edges with canonical semantic families and directions.

### Consequences

Traceability, impact analysis, queries, and generated views can operate over one model while object roles remain explicit.

### Confirmation

`TC-008` verifies the relation catalog and canonical semantic projection.
objects.title: Model traceability as a typed property graph

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

Separate graph-generation paths can cause the accessible static representation and the interactive Cytoscape view to disagree.

### Decision Outcome

Generate one bounded public projection and derive static diagram/table output and interactive exploration from that same artifact.

### Consequences

The public graph schema becomes a stable contract and interactive features must operate as progressive enhancement over it.

### Confirmation

`TC-006` validates the public projection contract and `TC-010` checks the exploration assets.
objects.title: Drive static and interactive graphs from the same projection

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

A multilingual book should not create two engineering graphs that can evolve independently.

### Decision Outcome

English QMD files are canonical engineering sources; `*.pt-BR.qmd` siblings may translate presentation text only. Pre-render validation rejects semantic differences.

### Consequences

Translations remain useful to readers while governance, baselines, impact analysis, and machine-readable exports stay language-neutral.

### Confirmation

`TC-005` checks semantic parity and localized title projection generation.
objects.title: Keep English canonical and localization presentation-only

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

Reimplementing query semantics in Lua would create another semantic authority and make graph views harder to reproduce.

### Decision Outcome

Named queries are evaluated by the Python core. Their result sets can be materialized as bounded graph views and consumed by shortcodes through a view manifest.

### Consequences

Selection remains deterministic and reusable across tables and graphs; presentation layers only request an already resolved view.

### Confirmation

`TC-009` verifies named-query graph materialization and manifest resolution.
objects.title: Evaluate named queries in the core and materialize reusable views

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

The page margin TOC can consume useful reading width, but a collapse control positioned over the TOC undermines the navigation it is intended to improve.

### Decision Drivers

- preserve native Quarto navigation semantics;
- make the feature optional and browser-only;
- persist the reader's collapsed state;
- reclaim content width while collapsed;
- never obscure the expanded TOC with the control itself.

### Decision Outcome

Implement the control as JavaScript progressive enhancement. Persist state in local storage, use Quarto's `fullcontent` class only while the extension forces the collapsed state, and position the expanded control completely outside the margin sidebar with an explicit gap.

### Consequences

The static document remains usable without JavaScript, while HTML readers gain a persistent space-reclaiming control. Positioning becomes an explicit regression contract rather than incidental CSS/DOM behavior.

### Confirmation

`TC-014` checks persistence/full-content behavior and verifies that the expanded control is positioned by `button.offsetWidth + gap`, never by the old half-width overlap.
objects.title: Treat the margin TOC control as persistent progressive enhancement
Keep the first OSLC federation path read-only, bounded, and cache-provenanced

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

A remote OSLC requirement can expose an identifier or title that happens to match a local object even when the two resources are unrelated. Automatically treating such similarity as identity would permit silent aliasing across independent authorities.

### Decision Drivers

- preserve external resource URI as the primary remote identity;
- make every bridge into canonical identity explicit and reviewable;
- reject stale or rejected observations before reconciliation;
- expose duplicate bindings and missing local targets as conflicts;
- keep comparison separate from mutation.

### Decision Outcome

Reconciliation is a pure analysis step. Only an explicit mapping from external resource URI to canonical Quarto-Needs ID can yield a matched item. External identifiers and titles are comparison data only. Unbound resources remain unbound, and field differences are reported without changing the snapshot.

### Consequences

This is intentionally more conservative than heuristic import. A future import command may consume an accepted reconciliation plan, but it cannot infer identity by itself and it cannot bypass provenance/trust checks.

### Confirmation

`TC-016` proves that a matching external identifier alone remains unbound and therefore cannot create an implicit canonical identity.
objects.title: Require explicit URI-to-canonical-ID bindings for OSLC reconciliation

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

GitHub's issues API returns pull requests alongside issues, rewrites pagination URLs from `/repos/{owner}/{repo}` to `/repositories/{id}` with cursor parameters, includes full inline issue data in list responses, and rate-limits clients with 403/429 responses. Treating any of those as canonical requirements data, following pagination without budgets, or flattening rate limits into generic errors would blur the trust boundary.

### Decision Drivers

- reuse OSLC's source-agnostic identity, observation, reconciliation, and import-plan contracts instead of forking them;
- keep discovered numbers separate from independently fetched, provenance-bound observations;
- validate server-provided pagination targets by origin, never by path, because GitHub legitimately rewrites its own Link targets;
- make truncation, malformed pagination, pull-request conflation, and rate-limit exhaustion explicit rather than guessed;
- keep the transport free of retry policy: report the server's retry facts and let the caller decide.

### Decision Outcome

GitHub federation is a read-only adapter composed of a bounded JSON transport with rate-limit classification, an opt-in content-addressed cache with conditional requests, issue/projection normalization that rejects pull requests, discovery and bounded multi-page traversal that stay numbers-only, and reconciliation/import planning through the unchanged OSLC contracts. List data is never promoted into observations; pagination targets are origin-checked; rate limits raise a distinguished, retry-informing error.

### Consequences

The adapter can discover, traverse, observe, reconcile, and plan imports safely before any synchronization exists. Canonical import and all remote writes remain deliberately deferred, and a rate-limit retry policy is caller-owned until a command needs one.

### Confirmation

`TC-020` exercises fetch-compose-normalize with exact-byte provenance; `TC-021` exercises the conditional-request 304 reuse path; `TC-022` exercises bounded traversal across GitHub's rewritten pagination targets with honest truncation; `TC-024` exercises rate-limit exhaustion classification against real header shapes.
objects.title: Keep the GitHub issues path read-only, bounded, and discovery-separated

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

`ARCHITECTURE.md` and this self-hosted example both describe the system, but neither page declares its audience, the concern it answers, or when it must be revisited. As the product grew from a single pipeline into CLI/core/Quarto/LSP/VS Code/interoperability surfaces, an undeclared set of ad hoc pages risks duplicating content and drifting silently.

### Decision Drivers

- give every architecture page an explicit audience, concern, and update trigger;
- avoid forcing one notation (C4, UML, or 4+1) to answer every question;
- keep the index navigable without becoming a second copy of this case study.

### Decision Outcome

Organize `notes/architecture/` as a small set of ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010-style viewpoints, indexed by an arc42-lite structure. Each page records its audience, concern, notation, and source in `viewpoints.md`; diagrams are chosen per concern rather than committing the whole set to one modeling language.

### Consequences

The documentation set gains a stable table of contents and a contract per page, at the cost of keeping `viewpoints.md` current whenever a page's purpose changes.

### Confirmation

`TC-002` confirms the presentation/rendering path this documentation set builds on.
objects.title: Document Quarto-Needs itself through explicit viewpoints, indexed arc42-lite

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

Phase 6 needed `system`/`container`/`component`/`actor`/`external-system` roles for C4 views. A fixed Python enum for architectural roles would hardcode one project's vocabulary into the core, contradicting the existing decision to keep traceability as a typed property graph with project-declared types (`ADR-003`).

### Decision Outcome

Architectural roles are ordinary entries under `[types.*]` in project configuration, validated the same way as every other type, never a hardcoded enumeration in `config.py`. `ARC001` and the C4 projection match on these configured types plus the fixed C4 layer order, never on a Python-level role constant.

### Consequences

A project can rename or extend its architectural vocabulary without a core code change; C4 support depends on a project actually declaring the expected types, which the C4 projection and `ARC001` already report explicitly when a focus type is unsupported.

### Confirmation

`TC-004` confirms decision and rule governance, including `ARC001`'s layer-adjacency checks.
objects.title: Model architectural roles as configurable types, not a fixed enumeration

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

`decomposes` already expressed parent-to-child containment, but nothing let a child self-declare its parent: every container had to enumerate its own components by hand, an error-prone, one-directional bookkeeping burden.

### Decision Outcome

Add `part-of` as `decomposes`'s genuine inverse (child-authored, `(part, whole)` roles, its own `v1_name` so `relation_policies` can target one direction independently). Enforce fixed-layer adjacency (`system > container > component > source-module`) with the `ARC001` rule over both authored directions.

### Consequences

Components and source modules author their own placement; `ARC001` catches layer-skipping or same-layer edges as a structural error, and non-C4 types are simply ignored by the rule rather than rejected.

### Confirmation

`TC-004`.
objects.title: Represent architecture hierarchy and containment through a first-class part-of relation

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

An external documentation-strategy review proposed adding an `ArchitectureElement realized-by ImplementationArtifact` relation (and its inverse `realizes`) to connect components to the source modules that implement them, reasoning that containment and "is realized by" are conceptually distinct. By the time this decision was recorded, `part-of` already connected every `source-module` to its owning `component` (see `implementation.qmd`), and `ARC001` already treats that edge as the bottom rung of the same fixed C4 layer ladder used for `container`/`system`.

### Considered Options

- introduce `realized-by`/`realizes` as a new relation family, kept parallel to `part-of`;
- keep `part-of` as the single relation connecting a source module to its owning component, exactly as it already connects a component to its container and a container to its system.

### Decision Outcome

Do not introduce `realized-by`/`realizes`. `part-of` already means "the child sits inside this parent at the next C4 layer up" for every layer, including `source-module -> component`. A second relation expressing the same fact between the same two objects would let the two edges disagree with no rule capable of detecting the contradiction, and would fragment `ARC001`'s single layer-adjacency check across two relation families.

### Consequences

Architecture-to-implementation traceability continues to read entirely through `part-of` plus `implements`/`implemented-by` (code to requirement); no new relation, rule, or projection code exists for this concern.

### Confirmation

`TC-004`.
objects.title: Reuse part-of instead of introducing a separate realized-by/realizes relation

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

A hand-maintained C4 diagram drifts the moment the underlying `part-of`/`depends-on` graph changes, and a second, independently authored diagram risks disagreeing with the engineering graph it claims to depict.

### Decision Outcome

`build_c4_view` computes every C4 level as one `select_graph` depth-1 call over an allowlisted set of relations for that level; `c4_mermaid_source`/`c4_code_table_markdown` render that projection as text; `write_c4_projections` writes one JSON file per view under `.quarto-needs/graphs/`. No C4 view is authored directly; the `need-c4` shortcode only ever reads a pre-rendered projection file.

### Consequences

Every C4 diagram in this documentation set is reproducible from the graph and cannot silently diverge from it; adding an object or `part-of` edge is sufficient to update the corresponding view on the next build.

### Confirmation

`TC-006`.
objects.title: Derive C4/architecture projections from the canonical snapshot, never hand-author them

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

C4/UML-flavored diagram text (Mermaid) is one presentation of the architecture graph; a second, unrelated presentation — the interactive Cytoscape exploration view — already exists over the same public projection.

### Decision Outcome

Mermaid source, the Code-level Markdown table, and the interactive Cytoscape view are alternate renderers over the same `graph_projection.py` output; none of them is treated as the canonical architecture model, and none of the three defines relation semantics of its own.

### Consequences

A future renderer (a different diagram language, a static image export) can consume the same projection without touching `analysis.py`, `relations.py`, or the C4 projection code.

### Confirmation

`TC-002`.
objects.title: Keep the architecture model renderer-independent

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

Generated files (`.quarto-needs/needs.json`, `.quarto-needs/graphs/*.json`, `generated-index.lua`) live inside the same project tree as authored `.qmd` declarations. Without an explicit rule, a contributor could hand-edit a generated file, or a generated file could be mistaken for a second authoring surface.

### Decision Outcome

Every path under a project's `.quarto-needs/` output directory is generated-only: the CLI build step recreates it in full on every run, `generated-index.lua` is explicitly excluded from the extension-asset sync so it is never treated as an authoring source, and stale `c4-*.json` files are removed before a projection is rewritten. `notes/architecture/generated/` follows the same rule for this documentation set's own diagrams.

### Consequences

Reviewers and contributors can rely on "is it under `.quarto-needs/` (or `notes/architecture/generated/`)?" as a sufficient test for "may I hand-edit this file?"; the answer is always no.

### Confirmation

`TC-006`.
objects.title: Draw an explicit boundary between authored architecture declarations and generated projections

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

This example's own `component` objects mix logical responsibility (parser, rule engine) with what are really deployable/executable units; a naive C4 projection that mapped every `type=component` to a C4 Component would blur the distinction between "runs as a process" and "is a logical piece of a process."

### Decision Outcome

`system` and `container` are configured as distinct types representing deployable/executable units; `component` remains the logical decomposition inside a container. `build_c4_view` requires a `system` focus for Context/Container and a `container` focus for Component, so a logical component can never itself be treated as a container boundary.

### Consequences

Adding a new deployable unit means declaring a new `container` (or `system`), not repurposing an existing `component`; `ARC001`'s fixed layer order (`system > container > component > source-module`) enforces this separation structurally.

### Confirmation

`TC-004`.
objects.title: Classify execution units (system, container) separately from logical components

objects.body:
### Context and Problem Statement

The extension needs a Python semantic engine, but users install only the extension. The old contract asked for three separate pieces — a global pip install, a CLI on PATH, and a hand-authored pre-render — each one an independent chance to be missing, stale, or wrong for the extension's version.

### Decision Outcome

The extension manifest contributes the project pre-render itself. A standard-library bootstrap provisions `quarto-needs==<extension version>` into `.quarto-needs/runtime/<version>/<interpreter-identity>/` through staged, lock-protected, atomic installs, validates the actually imported version, and invokes the same canonical pre-render service the CLI uses. A valid cached runtime renders offline; a provisioning failure fails the render with the needed version, the missing runtime, and both recovery actions.

### Consequences

Rendering has exactly one installation responsibility, and extension and engine versions cannot drift silently. First-use provisioning still requires Python and pip, which remain documented platform prerequisites; the residual availability risk is carried explicitly by `RISK-013` rather than hidden.

### Confirmation

`TC-025` proves the clean first render, `TC-026` the offline second render, and `TC-029` concurrent-safe provisioning.
objects.title: Provision a project-local managed runtime through an extension bootstrap

### Rationale

Provider identifiers and display fields can be reused, mutable, or locally ambiguous. Reconciliation must surface unbound resources, stale or rejected observations, missing local targets, duplicate bindings, and field differences before any future import operation is allowed.

objects.body:
Quarto-Needs shall execute a bounded HTTP GET against an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability, parse the query-result container deterministically, enforce a maximum member count, preserve query-response provenance, and report member URIs without recursively dereferencing them.

### Rationale

Discovery is not sufficient for practical federation, but query execution must not silently turn into unbounded Linked Data crawling. Query results therefore remain a resource-discovery projection; authoritative member observation is a separate bounded operation.
objects.rationale: Discovery is not sufficient for practical federation, but query execution must not silently turn into unbounded Linked Data crawling. Query results therefore remain a resource-discovery projection; authoritative member observation is a separate bounded operation.
objects.title: Execute an explicitly selected OSLC Query Capability without crawling members

objects.body:
Quarto-Needs shall fetch query-member URIs individually through the existing bounded transport/cache policy, normalize each fetched representation, enforce explicit fan-out and per-resource node limits, and create external requirement observations whose digest, retrieval time, trust state, validators, and resource identity derive from the bytes actually observed for that member.

### Rationale

A query container may include inline member data, but its response digest is not the digest of every member resource. Independent retrieval preserves the provenance boundary required for trustworthy reconciliation and any future reviewed import plan.
objects.rationale: A query container may include inline member data, but its response digest is not the digest of every member resource. Independent retrieval preserves the provenance boundary required for trustworthy reconciliation and any future reviewed import plan.
objects.title: Materialize selected OSLC query members as independently provenance-bearing observations

objects.body: The GitHub adapter shall normalize a fetched issue payload into an external requirement observation whose digest, retrieval time, and validators derive from the bytes actually fetched, reject pull requests explicitly, keep the issue number as data-only external identity, and treat null or missing fields without guessing.
objects.title: Normalize fetched GitHub issues without creating canonical identity

objects.body: The GitHub adapter shall compose the bounded GET-only transport with an opt-in content-addressed cache: a fresh cached representation shall skip the network entirely, a stale entry shall send conditional validators built from its own stored metadata, and a 304 response shall reuse the cached body under refreshed provenance instead of re-downloading it.
objects.title: Fetch GitHub issues through a bounded, cached, conditional transport

objects.body: The GitHub adapter shall report discovered issue and pull-request numbers separately for one bounded list page, follow the server-provided Link rel="next" target only within an explicit page budget and the request origin, report truncation honestly when the budget stops a traversal that could continue, fail loudly on malformed pagination headers, and never promote inline list data into provenance-bound observations.
objects.title: Discover and traverse issue-list pages within explicit budgets

objects.body: Observed GitHub issues shall reconcile and import-plan through the same source-agnostic reconciliation and reviewed import-plan contracts OSLC uses: an explicit external-API-URI to canonical-ID binding is the only identity bridge; a matching issue number, title, or HTML URL shall never create an implicit merge; and every planned directive remains a non-mutating review artifact carrying the observation's own provenance.
objects.title: Reconcile GitHub observations through the shared explicit-binding contracts

objects.body:
An active extension shall provision its exact paired engine version into a project-local runtime on first render, validate what it actually installed, and run the same canonical pre-render service the CLI uses.

### Rationale

Automatic exact provisioning removes the manual installation step and the extension/engine version-drift class of failure at once.
objects.rationale: Automatic exact provisioning removes the manual installation step and the extension/engine version-drift class of failure at once.
objects.title: Invoke an exact managed engine automatically during rendering

objects.body:
Ordinary rendering shall not require a quarto-needs package or a quarto-needs CLI on PATH, and a differently-versioned ambient installation shall never be substituted for the managed runtime.

### Rationale

A render's correctness cannot depend on whatever else happens to be installed on the machine.
objects.rationale: A render's correctness cannot depend on whatever else happens to be installed on the machine.

Interactive documentation must not become an accidental export channel for internal engineering data.

Interactivity must enhance the document rather than become the only way to access engineering information.

Large graphs can harm rendering, usability, and reviewability; failure should be explicit and reproducible.

Engineering meaning shall be resolved by the Python core; Lua and browser clients shall consume semantic projections and shall not redefine relation meaning.

Duplicated semantic maps create drift and make equivalent views disagree about the same engineering graph.

objects.body:
OSLC federation shall enforce byte/time/redirect/node/member budgets, reject cross-origin redirects, prevent implicit remote JSON-LD context loading and recursive member crawling, preserve content digests and historical observations, distinguish query-response provenance from member-resource provenance, and never hide authentication failures or identity conflicts behind stale cache fallback or heuristic matching.

### Rationale

External integration expands the trust boundary and therefore requires stronger failure, provenance, identity, and traversal contracts than local projection alone.
objects.rationale: External integration expands the trust boundary and therefore requires stronger failure, provenance, identity, and traversal contracts than local projection alone.

objects.body: GitHub federation shall enforce byte/time/redirect/page budgets, reject cross-origin redirect and pagination targets, and distinguish rate-limit exhaustion (a 403 carrying X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, or any 429) from authentication failures — reporting the server's retry facts to the caller instead of sleeping implicitly or hiding exhaustion behind generic errors.
objects.title: Keep GitHub federation bounded, provenance-preserving, and rate-limit-explicit

objects.body:
Managed runtime provisioning shall not modify the global Python environment, shall publish a runtime only after full validation, and shall remain safe under concurrent first renders.

### Rationale

A first render must never mutate anything outside the project or leave a half-installed runtime behind.
objects.rationale: A first render must never mutate anything outside the project or leave a half-installed runtime behind.
objects.title: Keep provisioning project-local, atomic, and concurrency-safe

objects.body:
Once a valid runtime exists, rendering shall reuse it without network access and without any provisioning attempt.

### Rationale

The package index is a first-render dependency only; everyday rendering must work offline.
objects.rationale: The package index is a first-render dependency only; everyday rendering must work offline.

Federation is useful only if remote state remains distinguishable from authored project truth and failures remain explainable.

GitHub issues carry engineering-relevant state, but the tracker is mutable, paginated, rate-limited, and mixes pull requests into its issue listings — federation therefore needs bounded budgets, exact-byte provenance, and explicit separation between discovery and observation.
